# tenzro-sdk API reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-api.cjs from the source. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every class and function `tenzro-sdk` exports. Methods that call the node name the JSON-RPC method; its params, result and errors are in the [JSON-RPC reference](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md).

## Classes

### AccessClient


|---|---|---|
| `did` | `string` |  |
| `dpopJkt` | `string` |  |

### AccountKeysClient

Operations on the keys of the signer's own account.

#### `enrollPqKey`

Enroll the hardware's ML-DSA-65 key as the account's post-quantum key, or replace the enrolled one. The hardware signs the proof of possession and the transaction; no key leaves it.

```ts
enrollPqKey(signer: HybridSigner): Promise<unknown>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `signer` | `HybridSigner` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<unknown>`

**Errors** Throws on invalid input.

#### `sendEnrolling`

Send `tx`; if the node answers that the account has no ML-DSA-65 key enrolled, enroll the hardware's key and send it again. An account signs nothing until it has enrolled one, so this is how a new account sends its first transaction.

```ts
sendEnrolling(signer: HybridSigner, tx: TypedTransaction): Promise<unknown>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `signer` | `HybridSigner` |  |
| `tx` | `TypedTransaction` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<unknown>`

**Errors** Throws on invalid input.

### AdaptiveBurnClient

Client for the adaptive-burn governance dial (TNZO supply control). Surfaces the current `BurnRateConfig`, rolling `SupplyMetricsSnapshot`, the recommended action computed from the targets and metrics, and the list of in-flight adaptive-burn governance proposals. All endpoints are read-only. The auto-proposal generator and the EIP-1559 fee-market consumer run inside the node alongside the governance executor; this client only reads their output.

#### `getBurnRateConfig`

Returns the current `BurnRateConfig` (base and local fee burn bps).

```ts
getBurnRateConfig(): Promise<any>
```

**Returns** `Promise<any>` Active burn-rate configuration

**Calls** [`tenzro_getBurnRateConfig`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_getburnrateconfig)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `getEconomicPolicy`

Returns the economic policy this node applies to every settlement — how a payment divides, the network's default settlement asset, and the micro-settlement floor. Read this before paying rather than inferring the split from a receipt afterwards. The response also reports, per capability, which economic mode the node is in: a **private** capability keeps the whole payment, a **public validating** one shares with the treasury, and a **public delegated** one also pays the RPC provider validating on its behalf. Every rate is governance-set; see `docs/ECONOMICS.md`.

```ts
getEconomicPolicy(): Promise<any>
```

**Returns** `Promise<any>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_getEconomicPolicy`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_geteconomicpolicy)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `getSupplyMetrics`

Returns the latest rolling supply metrics snapshot — circulating supply, epoch delta, burn breakdown, and supply added (always 0: TNZO supply is fixed at genesis; reported as `emission_breakdown`).

```ts
getSupplyMetrics(): Promise<any>
```

**Returns** `Promise<any>` Latest `SupplyMetricsSnapshot`

**Calls** [`tenzro_getSupplyMetrics`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_getsupplymetrics)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `getBurnRateRecommendation`

Computes the recommended adaptive-burn action from the current metrics and configured supply targets. May return `NoChange`, `IncreaseBurnPct`, `DecreaseBurnPct`, or alarm variants.

```ts
getBurnRateRecommendation(): Promise<any>
```

**Returns** `Promise<any>` `BurnRateRecommendation`

**Calls** [`tenzro_getBurnRateRecommendation`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_getburnraterecommendation)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `getFeeRate`

Returns the TNZO/USD rate fees are priced at (nano-USD per TNZO), its mode (`governance` or `validators`), its hourly rise and fall caps (`max_change_bps`, `max_fall_bps`), the safety rate safety checks value TNZO at (`safety_rate_nano_usd`), the next block's base fee in USD and in TNZO, and the settlement fee in basis points. With `symbol` (`ETH`, `SOL`, ...) it returns that asset's committed USD rate instead.

```ts
getFeeRate(symbol?: string): Promise<any>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `symbol` | `string \| undefined` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<any>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_getFeeRate`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_getfeerate)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `getEconomyMetrics`

Returns growth and concentration metrics for a reward epoch (the current one when `epoch` is omitted): settled value, payments per settlement, unique paying root identities, organic against unattributed volume, burn against rewards released from the pool, and the holder count, top-10 and top-100 share and Gini coefficient.

```ts
getEconomyMetrics(epoch?: number): Promise<any>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `epoch` | `number \| undefined` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<any>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_getEconomyMetrics`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_geteconomymetrics)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `listAdaptiveBurnProposals`

Burn-dial governance proposals, newest first: the policy updates that set the burn shares or the supply targets the dial steers by.

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `walletConsent`

### AgentClient

Client for AI agent operations. Supports agent registration, messaging, and task delegation.

#### `delegateTask`

Delegate a task to the node's A2A agent with an A2A v1.0 `SendMessage`.

```ts

```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `taskDescription` | `string` | Description of the task to delegate |

### AuthClient

Client for OAuth 2.1 + DPoP onboarding RPCs. Onboarding uses OAuth 2.1 (RFC 6749 successor) + DPoP-bound JWTs (RFC 9449) + Rich Authorization Requests (RFC 9396). Participants — humans, delegated agents under a human controller, and fully autonomous agents — onboard via the three RPCs exposed here. Each call provisions a TDIP identity (+ permissionless wallet) and returns a JWT bound to a holder-supplied DPoP `jkt` (RFC 7638 thumbprint of the holder's Ed25519 public key). Subsequent privileged calls (sign + send transaction, escrow create, release/refund, etc.) authenticate by sending the JWT in the `Authorization: DPoP <jwt>` header alongside a per-request DPoP proof in the `DPoP` header. The SDK forwards both headers automatically when the `TENZRO_BEARER_JWT` and `TENZRO_DPOP_PROOF` environment variables are set in Node — see {@link RpcClient} for the transport-level wiring.

#### `onboardHuman`

Onboard a new **human** participant — provisions a TDIP `did:tenzro:human:*` identity rooted in the caller's passkey, a permissionless wallet, and returns an OAuth 2.1 access token. The node only onboards a caller that proves it holds the passkey. This method requests the `enroll_passkey` custody challenge for exactly that passkey and hands it to `authorize`, which has the authenticator sign its `webauthn_challenge`. The SDK never sees the private key.

```ts
onboardHuman(displayName: string, credentialIdHex: string, publicKeyHex: string, authorize: (challenge: CustodyChallengeResponse) => Promise<CustodyAuthorization>, dpopJkt?: string): Promise<OnboardSession>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `displayName` | `string` | human-readable label surfaced in approver UIs |
| `credentialIdHex` | `string` | the passkey's credential id |
| `publicKeyHex` | `string` | the passkey's P-256 public key, raw `x \|\| y` or SEC1 uncompressed (`04 \|\| x \|\| y`) |
| `authorize` | `(challenge: CustodyChallengeResponse) => Promise<CustodyAuthorization>` | signs the issued challenge on the caller's authenticator; its `credential_id_hex` must be `credentialIdHex` |
| `dpopJkt` | `string \| undefined` | optional RFC 7638 JWK thumbprint of the holder's Ed25519 public key. If supplied, the issued JWT is DPoP-bound to that key and every subsequent privileged call must accompany the bearer with a fresh DPoP proof signed by the same key. Strongly recommended. |

**Returns** `Promise<OnboardSession>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_createCustodyChallenge`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_createcustodychallenge), [`tenzro_onboardHuman`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_onboardhuman)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `onboardDelegatedAgent`

Onboard a **machine** as a delegated agent of an existing `controllerDid` (a human). The machine's key lives in its TPM or Secure Enclave; `devicePublicKeyHex` is its public half. The controller approves the machine's terms, with its hardware key as the single serving node, through a `delegate_agent` custody challenge on their smart account; `authorize` signs it with a passkey enrolled there.

```ts
onboardDelegatedAgent(accountAddress: string, controllerDid: string, devicePublicKeyHex: string, machineId: string, capabilities: string[], delegationScope: unknown, authorize: (challenge: CustodyChallengeResponse) => Promise<RootAuthorization>, dpopJkt?: string): Promise<OnboardSession>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `accountAddress` | `string` |  |
| `controllerDid` | `string` |  |
| `devicePublicKeyHex` | `string` |  |
| `machineId` | `string` |  |
| `capabilities` | `string[]` |  |
| `delegationScope` | `unknown` |  |
| `authorize` | `(challenge: CustodyChallengeResponse) => Promise<RootAuthorization>` |  |
| `dpopJkt` | `string \| undefined` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<OnboardSession>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_createCustodyChallenge`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_createcustodychallenge), [`tenzro_onboardDelegatedAgent`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_onboarddelegatedagent)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `delegateAgent`

Delegate an agent with its root's approval: a human's passkey, or a machine's hardware key (machineRootAuthorization). `terms` names the controller, the agent, its scope and limits, its capabilities, its serving nodes as `[{machine_did, operator_did}]`, `min_distinct_operators` and `expires_at_ms`. The node completes each serving node's key and returns a challenge over the completed terms; `authorize` signs it with a passkey enrolled on the controller's smart account. The serving nodes deliver the agent's access tokens; the result says how each delivery went.

```ts
delegateAgent(accountAddress: string, terms: AgentTerms, authorize: (challenge: CustodyChallengeResponse) => Promise<RootAuthorization>): Promise<DelegatedAgent>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `accountAddress` | `string` |  |
| `terms` | `AgentTerms` |  |
| `authorize` | `(challenge: CustodyChallengeResponse) => Promise<RootAuthorization>` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<DelegatedAgent>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_createCustodyChallenge`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_createcustodychallenge), [`tenzro_onboardDelegatedAgent`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_onboarddelegatedagent)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

Replace a delegated agent's terms with the controller's passkey. The agent's DID stays the same; with `rotateTokens` set, its live access tokens are withdrawn and the result counts them.

```ts
updateAgentTerms(accountAddress: string, agentDid: string, terms: AgentTerms, rotateTokens: boolean, authorize: (challenge: CustodyChallengeResponse) => Promise<RootAuthorization>): Promise<AgentTermsUpdate>
```

|---|---|---|
| `accountAddress` | `string` |  |
| `agentDid` | `string` |  |
| `terms` | `AgentTerms` |  |
| `rotateTokens` | `boolean` |  |

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `revokeIdentity`

Revoke an identity with its root's approval (a passkey, or a machine's hardware key): a root revokes itself, a delegated agent is revoked by the controller its terms name, and a machine a root registered by that root. `accountAddress` is the approving root's account and `approverDid` the root (`did` itself by default). `approve` signs the `revoke_identity` challenge, which covers `did` and `reason`, and returns the root's key and signature ({@link passkeyRootApproval}, {@link machineRootApproval}). The SDK puts the approval into a `RevokeIdentity` transaction, signs it with `signer` (any account may send it; the approval authorises it) and submits it with `tenzro_revokeIdentity`. Every validator re-verifies the approval; once the transaction is in a block every node treats the identity as revoked and revokes its tokens, and revoking a root also revokes every agent it delegated.

```ts
revokeIdentity(signer: HybridSigner, accountAddress: string, did: string, approve: (challenge: CustodyChallengeResponse) => Promise<RootApproval>, options?: { approverDid?: string; reason?: string; }): Promise<RevokeResponse>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `signer` | `HybridSigner` |  |
| `accountAddress` | `string` |  |
| `did` | `string` |  |
| `approve` | `(challenge: CustodyChallengeResponse) => Promise<RootApproval>` |  |
| `options` | `{ approverDid?: string; reason?: string; }` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<RevokeResponse>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_createCustodyChallenge`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_createcustodychallenge), [`tenzro_revokeIdentity`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_revokeidentity)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `onboardAutonomousAgent`

Onboard a **fully autonomous agent**, rooted in its own secure element: `devicePublicKey` (hex) and the `machineId` of the element holding it. It has no human controller; instead its bond must already be locked on chain: an active `PostAgentBond` of at least 1 TNZO for the DID the device key derives.

```ts
onboardAutonomousAgent(devicePublicKey: string, machineId: string, dpopJkt?: string): Promise<OnboardSession>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `devicePublicKey` | `string` |  |
| `machineId` | `string` |  |
| `dpopJkt` | `string \| undefined` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<OnboardSession>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_onboardAutonomousAgent`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_onboardautonomousagent)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `refreshToken`

Exchange a long-lived refresh token for a fresh access token. Mirrors OAuth 2.1 `grant_type=refresh_token`. Refresh tokens are opaque UUIDs with a 30-day TTL; access tokens are ES256 JWTs with a 1-hour TTL. `prover` holds the key the refresh token is bound to and proves it for this request; a refresh token issued without a key is bound to it from now on. Each refresh token is good for one exchange: keep the `refresh_token` the answer carries for the next one.

```ts
refreshToken(refreshToken: string, prover: DpopProver): Promise<RefreshedToken>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `refreshToken` | `string` |  |
| `prover` | `DpopProver` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<RefreshedToken>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_refreshToken`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_refreshtoken)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `revokeJwt`

Revoke a single JWT by its `jti` claim. The token is added to the engine's revocation set and any subsequent validation fails. `didEnvelope` is the hex envelope proving control of the token's bearer DID **or** of the controller DID that authorized it, bound to method `tenzro_revokeJwt` with the `jti` bytes as the params hash. A `jti` travels in every audit row, so it is an identifier, not a credential.

```ts
revokeJwt(jti: string, didEnvelope: string, reason?: string): Promise<RevokeResponse>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `jti` | `string` |  |
| `didEnvelope` | `string` |  |
| `reason` | `string \| undefined` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<RevokeResponse>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_revokeJwt`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_revokejwt)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `forgetIdentity`

TDIP/GDPR Article 17 right-to-erasure. Hard-deletes a previously revoked identity from the registry and persistent storage. The identity MUST already be `Revoked` — call {@link revokeIdentity} first, wait for its transaction to land, and then call this. Distinct from `revokeIdentity`, which is a logical delete.

```ts
forgetIdentity(did: string): Promise<{ did: string; status: string; note: string; }>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `did` | `string` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<{ did: string; status: string; note: string; }>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_forgetIdentity`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_forgetidentity)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `exchangeToken`

**RFC 8693 OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange.** Exchange a parent JWT for a narrower child JWT bound to a different DPoP key, with a strictly subset of the parent's RAR grants and AAP capabilities. The child token's `controller_did` is set to the parent's `sub`, extending the act-chain by one hop. Subset enforcement is performed by the AS — `requestedRar` and `requestedAapCapabilities` must be a strict subset of what the parent already holds. Anything outside the parent's authority is rejected with JSON-RPC error code `-32002`.

```ts
exchangeToken(subjectToken: string, childBearerDid: string, childDpopJkt: string, requestedRar: unknown, requestedAapCapabilities: unknown[], requestedTtlSecs?: number): Promise<TokenExchangeResult>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `subjectToken` | `string` | the parent JWT (validated for signature, exp, and revocation by the AS) |
| `childBearerDid` | `string` | DID that will be the `sub` of the child JWT |
| `childDpopJkt` | `string` | RFC 7638 JWK thumbprint of the child holder's Ed25519 public key. The child token will be DPoP-bound to it. |
| `requestedRar` | `unknown` | typed scope envelope (RFC 9396) the child should carry. Must be a subset of the parent's `authorization_details`. |
| `requestedAapCapabilities` | `unknown[]` | AAP `aap_capabilities` claim list. Must be a subset of the parent's capabilities. |
| `requestedTtlSecs` | `number \| undefined` | optional override; clamped to the engine's `max_ttl_secs` and parent's remaining lifetime. |

**Returns** `Promise<TokenExchangeResult>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_exchangeToken`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_exchangetoken)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `introspectToken`

**RFC 7662 OAuth 2.0 Token Introspection.** Ask the AS whether a token is currently active and, if so, return its full claim set (RAR, AAP, cnf, controller_did, etc.). Per RFC 7662 §2.2 a failed validation returns `{ active: false }` with no other fields — the AS deliberately does not leak why the token is inactive. Use this from a downstream resource server that wants to validate a bearer token without re-implementing JWT signature checking.

```ts
introspectToken(token: string): Promise<IntrospectionResult>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `token` | `string` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<IntrospectionResult>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_introspectToken`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_introspecttoken)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `oauthDiscovery`

**RFC 8414 / RFC 9728 OAuth Authorization Server / Protected Resource Metadata.** Returns the same metadata document the AS publishes at `GET /.well-known/openid-configuration`. Useful for JSON-RPC-only clients (CLI, agents) that don't want to also speak HTTP discovery.

```ts
oauthDiscovery(): Promise<OAuthDiscovery>
```

**Returns** `Promise<OAuthDiscovery>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_oauthDiscovery`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_oauthdiscovery)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

### BondClient

Client for AgentBond operations. Bonds are TNZO-denominated stakes posted by a controller against a specific agent DID. While Active and ≥ `bond_min_for_promotion`, the bonded agent is promoted to the Delegated admission lane. Bonds are locked at a deterministic vault address derived from the agent DID: `Address(SHA-256("tenzro/agent-bond/vault" || agent_did))`. Read methods query node state directly. Write methods build typed `PostAgentBond` / `IncreaseAgentBond` / `WithdrawAgentBond` transactions and submit them through `tenzro_sendRawTransaction`, matching the {@link SettlementClient.createEscrow } pattern.

### DeviceClient

Devices bound to a Tenzro identity, and machine ownership. A Tenzro identity links devices the way a platform account does, except the link is not a platform account. No Apple, Google or Microsoft sign-in is an identity authority here: what the node trusts is a WebAuthn attestation it verifies to a vendor root it pins, so "hardware-bound" is a fact the device proved rather than a claim its cloud account made. A wallet cannot sit behind one device. `walletReadiness` reports whether a second bound device exists yet, and names the remedy when it does not.

#### `challenge`

The single-use custody challenge a device change answers: `bind_device` for `(identityDid, label)`, `revoke_device` for `(identityDid, credentialId)`, `transfer_machine_ownership` for `(machineDid, newOwnerDid)`. A registration signs `challenge_hex` as its WebAuthn challenge; an assertion from a bound device signs `webauthn_challenge`.

```ts
challenge(operation: "bind_device" | "revoke_device" | "transfer_machine_ownership", accountDid: string, target: string): Promise<CustodyChallengeResponse>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `operation` | `"bind_device" \| "revoke_device" \| "transfer_machine_ownership"` |  |
| `accountDid` | `string` |  |
| `target` | `string` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<CustodyChallengeResponse>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_createCustodyChallenge`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_createcustodychallenge)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `bindDevice`

Bind a device to an identity from a WebAuthn registration made over a `bind_device` challenge for `(identity_did, label)`. The node grades the attestation against the vendor roots it pins: a device whose key is not in hardware, or whose credential can sync to a cloud account, is refused with the reason. The first device must be the identity's own passkey; another needs `authorization`, an assertion from a device already bound.

```ts
bindDevice(request: BindDeviceRequest): Promise<BoundDevice>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `request` | `BindDeviceRequest` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<BoundDevice>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_bindDevice`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_binddevice)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `listBoundDevices`

The devices that can authenticate as an identity, and what each proved.

```ts
listBoundDevices(identityDid: string): Promise<BoundDevices>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `identityDid` | `string` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<BoundDevices>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_listBoundDevices`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_listbounddevices)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `revokeBoundDevice`

Unbind a device and end every session it authorised, in one action. `authorization` is an assertion from a bound device over a `revoke_device` challenge for `(identityDid, credentialId)`.

```ts
revokeBoundDevice(identityDid: string, credentialId: string, challengeId: string, authorization: DeviceAssertion): Promise<DeviceRevocation>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `identityDid` | `string` |  |
| `credentialId` | `string` |  |
| `challengeId` | `string` |  |
| `authorization` | `DeviceAssertion` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<DeviceRevocation>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_revokeBoundDevice`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_revokebounddevice)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `walletReadiness`

Whether a wallet may be created for this identity, and if not, why. Read before offering wallet creation so the user is told what to do, "scan the pairing QR with your phone", rather than shown a button that fails. A wallet cannot sit behind a single device.

```ts
walletReadiness(identityDid: string, thisDeviceCredentialId?: string): Promise<WalletReadiness>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `identityDid` | `string` |  |
| `thisDeviceCredentialId` | `string \| undefined` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<WalletReadiness>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_walletReadiness`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_walletreadiness)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `transferMachineOwnership`

Move a machine to another identity, answering a `transfer_machine_ownership` challenge for `(machineDid, newOwnerDid)`. A `controller` authority carries an assertion from a device bound to the controller of a machine a party delegated; a `machine_key` authority the machine's own signature over the challenge, for a machine nobody delegated. The two are not interchangeable.

```ts
transferMachineOwnership(machineDid: string, newOwnerDid: string, challengeId: string, authority: TransferAuthority): Promise<Record<string, unknown>>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `machineDid` | `string` |  |
| `newOwnerDid` | `string` |  |
| `challengeId` | `string` |  |
| `authority` | `TransferAuthority` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<Record<string, unknown>>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_transferMachineOwnership`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_transfermachineownership)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

The rails a payment can settle on, and the smallest worthwhile payment on each. Supporting x402 and being able to carry a micropayment are different properties — Base speaks x402 and still cannot carry a one-cent charge without ~10% overhead.

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `routePayment`

Where a specific charge would settle: accumulate below the micro-settlement floor, the Tenzro Ledger, a secondary rail, or no viable rail for the payee's asset. Omit `tnzoMicroUsd` and the node settles on the home chain rather than routing on a guessed rate.

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

### EventsClient

Client for the chain's events: follow them from a cursor, query ranges with proofs. Verify proofs with `verifyEventProof`.

#### `subscribe`

The next events `filter` selects after `fromCursor` (from the tip when omitted), waiting up to `waitMs` for new blocks. Pass the returned cursor back: a reader that restarts resumes with no gap and no repeat. With `proofs`, each event carries the proof `verifyEventProof` checks.

```ts
subscribe(filter: EventFilter, fromCursor?: string, waitMs?: number, proofs?: boolean): Promise<EventPage>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `filter` | `EventFilter` |  |
| `fromCursor` | `string \| undefined` |  |
| `waitMs` | `number` |  |
| `proofs` | `boolean` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<EventPage>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_subscribe`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_subscribe)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `query`

A page of the events `filter` selects after `fromCursor`, each with its proof. With `completeness`, also the proof that the page left nothing out (check it with `verifyCompleteness`), every proof anchored at `anchorIndex` or at the latest certified checkpoint.

| `anchorIndex` | `number \| undefined` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<EventPage>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_queryEvents`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_queryevents)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

### FailoverTransport

A transport over several endpoints: each call goes to the current one and moves to the next when it cannot be reached, times out or answers with an HTTP error. A JSON-RPC error is the node's answer and is returned as is. It carries no access credential, so it serves open methods and signed transactions, which every operator accepts on their own signature.

#### `endpoint`

Read-only `string`. The endpoint calls go to now.

#### `call`

```ts
call<T>(method: string, params?: unknown[] | Record<string, unknown>): Promise<T>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `method` | `string` |  |
| `params` | `unknown[] \| Record<string, unknown>` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<T>`

**Errors** Throws on invalid input.

### IdentityClient

Client for Tenzro Decentralized Identity Protocol (TDIP) operations. Supports both human and machine identities with W3C DID documents.

#### `registerHuman`

Register a human identity bound to a passkey (`tenzro_registerIdentity` with `identity_type` `human`). `publicKey` is the passkey's P-256 key and `credentialId` its credential id (both hex); `proof` is the passkey's composite signature over the registration statement under the `IdentityRegistration` context, which the node requires. Applications enrolling a passkey from a browser use `PasskeyRpcClient.enroll` instead, which takes the WebAuthn registration as it comes.

```ts
registerHuman(params: { displayName: string; publicKey: string; credentialId: string; proof: Record<string, unknown>; }): Promise<RegisterIdentityResult>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `params` | `{ displayName: string; publicKey: string; credentialId: string; proof: Record<string, unknown>; }` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<RegisterIdentityResult>` The DID and the hash of the `RegisterIdentity` transaction that replicates it. The node records nothing when it cannot submit that transaction, and the call fails instead.

**Calls** [`tenzro_registerIdentity`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_registeridentity)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `registerMachine`

Register a machine identity under a controller (`tenzro_registerMachineIdentity`). The machine acts for its controller, carries its delegation scope and draws on its admission quota, so the controller signs the request: `controller` is the controller's own passkey, TPM or Secure Enclave signer, and the request carries its DID envelope over every field. The node refuses a request without one, or with one from any other DID.

```ts
registerMachine(params: { controllerDid: string; publicKey: string; capabilities: string[]; }, controller: HybridSigner): Promise<IdentityInfo>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `params` | `{ controllerDid: string; publicKey: string; capabilities: string[]; }` |  |
| `controller` | `HybridSigner` | Signer holding the key `controllerDid` resolves to |

**Returns** `Promise<IdentityInfo>` The machine's DID, its controller, status and capabilities

**Calls** [`tenzro_registerMachineIdentity`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_registermachineidentity)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

**Returns** `Promise<IdentityInfo>` Identity information

#### `joinAsMicroNode`

Join the Tenzro Network as a MicroNode participant. Zero-install — no P2P binary required. Provisions a TDIP DID and a wallet bound to the caller's identity key: the P-256 public key (x || y, hex) with the passkey `credential_id` of a human, or the `machine_id` of a secure-element key. The node never mints a key.



Request inference from a specific model.

```ts
request(modelId: string, input: string, maxTokens?: number): Promise<InferenceResult>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `modelId` | `string` | The model identifier |
| `input` | `string` | The input text/data |
| `maxTokens` | `number \| undefined` | Optional maximum tokens to generate (default: 1024) |

**Returns** `Promise<InferenceResult>` Inference result with output, cost, and metadata

**Calls** [`tenzro_inferenceRequest`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_inferencerequest)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `routeIntent`

Resolve an intent to the best model without naming one. Discovery only: no provider is dialed and no spend is recorded, but the per-DID budget gate and the wallet-balance ceiling are still consulted, so an unaffordable request is rejected at discovery time. Feed the returned `model_id` into {@link request} or the chat surface to run it.

```ts
routeIntent(params: IntentParams): Promise<RouteDecision>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `params` | `IntentParams` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<RouteDecision>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_routeIntent`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_routeintent)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `recordRouteOutcome`

Report how a routed call turned out, so per-cluster error rates reflect what happened rather than only what the catalog declares. `cluster` is the `cluster` from the routing decision. In practice this carries `escalated` — the outcome only the caller knows, because it means the caller took the answer to a stronger model. `resolved` and `failed` are already recorded by {@link chatByIntent} from the dispatch itself. Reporting is advisory: `retained: false` in the response means the node has no difficulty index wired, so the feedback was accepted and discarded.

```ts
recordRouteOutcome(modelId: string, cluster: number, outcome: RouteOutcome): Promise<Record<string, unknown>>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `modelId` | `string` |  |
| `cluster` | `number` |  |
| `outcome` | `RouteOutcome` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<Record<string, unknown>>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_recordRouteOutcome`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_recordrouteoutcome)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `routeDifficultyStats`

Read the node's difficulty index: how many clusters it has discovered and how many prompts landed in each. With `modelId`, also returns that model's per-cluster outcome counters and error rate. An operator diagnostic — routing does not depend on it.

```ts
routeDifficultyStats(modelId?: string): Promise<Record<string, unknown>>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `modelId` | `string \| undefined` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<Record<string, unknown>>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_routeDifficultyStats`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_routedifficultystats)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

```ts
chatByIntent(params: IntentParams & { message?: string; messages?: Array<{ role: string; content: string; }>; }): Promise<Record<string, unknown>>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `params` | `IntentParams & { message?: string; messages?: Array<{ role: string; content: string; }>; }` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<Record<string, unknown>>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_chatByIntent`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_chatbyintent)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `getProvenance`

Look up the cached provenance manifest for generated content by its 32-byte hex `contentHash` (with or without `0x` prefix). This is the machine-readable synthetic-content marker per EU AI Act Art. 50(2). Throws JSON-RPC `-32004` when no manifest is cached for the hash.

```ts
getProvenance(contentHash: string): Promise<Record<string, unknown>>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `contentHash` | `string` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<Record<string, unknown>>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_getContentProvenance`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_getcontentprovenance)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `getGeneration`

Read back what one finished generation consumed and cost, by the id you already hold — a `chatcmpl-…` from a chat completion, or the `request_id` of a routed inference. Useful when a stream was consumed and the terminal chunk went by, or when reconciling a billing period against your own request log. Throws JSON-RPC `-32004` when the id is unknown to this node, which also covers a generation still running or one that failed before it could be recorded.

```ts

```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `string` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<GenerationStats>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_getGeneration`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_getgeneration)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `listInferenceUsage`

Read usage. Which tier comes back follows the filters given: pass both a model and a provider for the matching records, one for that model's or provider's rollup, neither for the global rollup plus the per-model and per-provider breakdowns. Records are the node's bounded ring of recent generations; the rollups are lifetime totals that survive restart.

```ts
listInferenceUsage(filters?: { modelId?: string; provider?: string; }): Promise<InferenceUsage>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `filters` | `{ modelId?: string; provider?: string; } \| undefined` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<InferenceUsage>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_listInferenceUsage`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_listinferenceusage)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

| `newPasskey` | `HybridSigner` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<KeystoreUpdate>`

**Errors** Throws on invalid input.

#### `send`

Send `update`, signed and paid for by `sender`. With `fromAccount`, the transaction is sent from that account (the passkey account itself, so the sender's passkey also approves); otherwise from the account the sender's key names: a sponsor (a wallet provider, or a friend) that pays the fee of an account with no balance and authorizes nothing, the change carrying the passkeys' approvals. The fee is paid at `gasPrice`, or at the node's current price (`eth_gasPrice`).

```ts
send(sender: HybridSigner, update: KeystoreUpdate, fromAccount?: string, gasPrice?: number): Promise<unknown>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `sender` | `HybridSigner` |  |
| `update` | `KeystoreUpdate` |  |
| `fromAccount` | `string \| undefined` |  |
| `gasPrice` | `number \| undefined` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<unknown>`

**Errors** Throws on invalid input.

### LedgerPayments

Quote, pay and verify ledger payments over one or more node endpoints.

#### `quote`

What `price` costs in each of `accept` now, with the fee each pays in kind and, through `resellers`, the operator's price and each commission disclosed apart; chooses the first that can settle.

```ts
quote(q: { payee: string; price: Price; request: string; accept: string[]; resellers?: ResellerCommission[]; }): Promise<LedgerQuote>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `q` | `{ payee: string; price: Price; request: string; accept: string[]; resellers?: ResellerCommission[]; }` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<LedgerQuote>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_quotePayment`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_quotepayment)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `pay`

Pays a quote: signs the authorization for the chosen asset and amount, has a node relay it, and waits for the record. A retry with the same idempotency key looks the payment up first and never pays twice.

```ts
pay(q: LedgerQuote, o: PayOptions): Promise<LedgerReceipt>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `q` | `LedgerQuote` |  |
| `o` | `PayOptions` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<LedgerReceipt>`

**Calls** [`eth_chainId`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#eth_chainid), [`tenzro_settle`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_settle)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `verifyReceipt`

Checks a payment's record on two endpoints.

```ts
verifyReceipt(r: Omit<LedgerReceipt, "record"> & { record?: unknown; }): Promise<LedgerReceipt>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `r` | `Omit<LedgerReceipt, "record"> & { record?: unknown; }` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<LedgerReceipt>`

**Errors** Throws on invalid input.

#### `payFor`

Quote, pay and verify in one call, through `resellers` when given.

```ts
payFor(request: string, o: PayOptions & { payee: string; price: Price; accept: string[]; resellers?: ResellerCommission[]; }): Promise<LedgerReceipt>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `request` | `string` |  |
| `o` | `PayOptions & { payee: string; price: Price; accept: string[]; resellers?: ResellerCommission[]; }` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<LedgerReceipt>`

**Errors** Throws on invalid input.

#### `charge`

Seller side: serves `handler` only for a request whose payment id names a payment on chain to `payee` worth at least `price` for that request, checked on two endpoints, and only the first time that payment is presented (`store`, by default this wrapper's memory); otherwise answers 402 with what to pay.

```ts
charge<Req extends { request: string; paymentId?: string; }, Res>(handler: (req: Req, receipt: Record<string, unknown>) => Promise<Res>, o: { payee: string; price: Price; accept: string[]; store?: ChargeStore; reseller?: ResellerCommission; }): (req: Req) => Promise<Res | { status: 402; reason?: "payment_consumed"; payment: { payee: string; price: Price; accept: string[]; request: string; }; }>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `handler` | `(req: Req, receipt: Record<string, unknown>) => Promise<Res>` |  |
| `o` | `{ payee: string; price: Price; accept: string[]; store?: ChargeStore; reseller?: ResellerCommission; }` |  |

**Returns** `(req: Req) => Promise<Res \| { status: 402; reason?: "payment_consumed"; payment: { payee: string; price: Price; accept: string[]; request: string; }; }>`

**Errors** Throws on invalid input.

### LifecycleClient

The kill-switch records every `TerminateAgent` event — including cascaded terminations from a parent agent — with the canonical reason code, the slash applied to the bond, and the controller that authorised it. ### MachineAccessClient

Machine access: what a machine's owner lets agents, tools and models on a node reach. Nothing on a node can reach its loopback services, its LAN, cloud metadata endpoints or host folders unless the machine's owner signed a grant for it. Every change is signed by the owner in two steps: `challenge` returns a custody challenge bound to exactly the change; the owner approves it in their wallet (a passkey assertion and an ML-DSA-65 signature over the digest); the approval, with `challenge_id` set, goes to `add`, `list` or `revoke` as `authorization`.

#### `challenge`

Issue the custody challenge for `change`. Returns `challenge_id`, `webauthn_challenge` (what the owner's passkey signs) and the owner's `account_address`. Terms the node would refuse are refused here, before anyone signs them.

```ts
challenge(change: MachineAccessChange): Promise<any>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `change` | `MachineAccessChange` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<any>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_createCustodyChallenge`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_createcustodychallenge)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `add`

Add a grant with exactly the terms the challenge was issued for.

```ts
add(terms: MachineAccessTerms, authorization: unknown): Promise<any>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `terms` | `MachineAccessTerms` |  |
| `authorization` | `unknown` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<any>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_addMachineAccess`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_addmachineaccess)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `list`

The grants on the node, with their use, refusal and byte counts.


|---|---|---|
| `authorization` | `unknown` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<any>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_listMachineAccess`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_listmachineaccess)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

Revoke a grant. It stops applying at once.

### MultimodalClient

Multi-modal AI client — covers the ONNX-backed runtimes on a Tenzro node: forecast (timeseries), vision encoders, text embeddings, click-driven segmentation, text-promptable segmentation, detection, audio (ASR), and video. Each modality has the same surface shape: `list{Modality}Catalog()` to browse curated models, `load{Modality}Model()` to bring a model online, `unload{Modality}Model()` to drop it, and one inference verb. `InferenceClient.listLoadedModels()` lists what is loaded, of every type. Every catalog loader takes the same `LoadModelParams`: the catalog model id and an optional visibility. The node fetches and verifies the files the signed catalog entry names, and enforces the entry's licence tier: it refuses with JSON-RPC `-32010` when the operator has not accepted that entry's terms. Those are node-operator startup flags, never client parameters. The runtimes are feature-gated. A node built without the `onnx` feature answers every load and inference call with JSON-RPC `-32011`.

#### `rerank`

#### `transcribeStream`

Transcribe live audio as it is captured, over the realtime transport. `chunks` yields mono 16-bit little-endian PCM. Yields `partial` transcripts of the open segment, `final` segments committed at pauses (each billed by the second of audio and receipted), then `done`. The node must serve the model.

```ts
transcribeStream(params: { model_id: string; sample_rate?: number; language?: string; verification?: TaskRouting["verification"]; }, chunks: AsyncIterable<Uint8Array> | Iterable<Uint8Array>): AsyncGenerator<{ event: string; data: unknown; }>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `params` | `{ model_id: string; sample_rate?: number; language?: string; verification?: TaskRouting["verification"]; }` |  |
| `chunks` | `AsyncIterable<Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>> \| Iterable<Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>>` |  |

**Returns** `AsyncGenerator<{ event: string; data: unknown; }, any, any>`

**Errors** Throws on invalid input.

Ask the node for the challenge an already-enrolled passkey must sign to authorize one custody change. Single-use and time-bounded, bound to this account and this operation. ### PaymentClient

Client for payment challenges, credential checks and ledger settlement.

#### `createChallenge`

Create a payment challenge for a resource (payee side). The node stamps it with its chain id; the payer signs a credential for it.

```ts
createChallenge(resource: string, amount: bigint | number, asset?: string, protocol?: string, recipient?: string): Promise<PaymentChallenge>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `resource` | `string` | Resource identifier (e.g., URL or model ID) |
| `amount` | `number \| bigint` | Payment amount, in the asset's smallest unit |
| `asset` | `string` | Asset identifier (default: "TNZO") |
| `protocol` | `string` | Payment protocol: "mpp" or "x402" (default: "mpp") |
| `recipient` | `string \| undefined` | Payee address (default: the node's payee) |

**Returns** `Promise<PaymentChallenge>` The challenge, as the node issued it

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.


| Param | Type | Description |

| `q` | `{ usdE6?: number \| bigint; price?: { amount: string; unit: "USD"; }; accept?: string[]; }` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<{ usd_e6: number \| bigint; unit: { basket: string; version: number; }; rate_epoch: number \| null; assets: Record<string, unknown>[]; }>`

### ProviderClient

Client for provider operations including network participation, model serving, and hardware management.

#### `serveModel`

Start serving a model on the network. When a model is too large for a single host, the node auto-clusters: it reads the GGUF header for layer count and hidden dimension, discovers LAN members from gossiped cluster announcements, and runs a layer-wise pipeline across them. No extra options are required — the node decides single-host vs. cluster from the model shape and the reachable members. Pass `opts` to set: - `visibility`: `"public"`, `"gated"` or `"private"` for this model. Omitted, the model follows the node's visibility. - `maxConcurrent`: the concurrent requests admitted for this model. - `loadDrafter`: `false` skips loading the catalog drafter for multi-token prediction. Use {@link Discovery.clusterPlan } to preview the layer split and {@link ProviderClient.previewServe} to preview the memory it takes.

```ts
serveModel(modelId: string, opts?: ServeOptions): Promise<void>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `modelId` | `string` | ID of the model to serve |
| `opts` | `ServeOptions` | Optional visibility and concurrency settings |

**Returns** `Promise<void>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_serveModel`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_servemodel)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

```typescript
await client.provider.serveModel("gemma4-9b");
console.log("Now serving model");
```

```typescript
  if (ep.load) {
    console.log(`  Load: ${ep.load.active_requests}/${ep.load.max_concurrent} (${ep.load.utilization_percent}%)`);
  }
}
```


#### `listProviders`

List all providers discovered on the Tenzro Network. Queries the `tenzro_listProviders` JSON-RPC method which merges: - The local node's own provider info (if it is serving models) - All remote providers discovered via the `tenzro/providers` gossipsub topic (announcements refreshed every 60 seconds)

```ts
listProviders(providerType?: string): Promise<NetworkProvider[]>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `providerType` | `string \| undefined` | Optional filter by provider class (e.g. "ai", "tee", "storage"), applied to the node's full list. |

**Returns** `Promise<NetworkProvider[]>` Array of discovered network providers

**Calls** [`tenzro_listProviders`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_listproviders)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

```typescript
// List all providers
const providers = await client.provider.listProviders();
for (const p of providers) {
  console.log(`${p.endpoint_id}:${p.provider_type} — models: ${p.served_models.join(", ")}`);
}

// List only model providers
const aiProviders = await client.provider.listProviders("ai");
```

### RpcCallError

A JSON-RPC error the node answered with: its `code`, message and `data`. -32602 is invalid params, -32601 an unknown method, -32004 a resource or capability this node does not have.

#### `isLightBuild`

Read-only `boolean`. True when the node is the light build of tenzro-node, which runs no model: it refuses a call that needs a local model with code -32004 and `data.build === "light"`. Send such a call to a provider node instead.

### RpcClient

JSON-RPC and HTTP client for one node. A client carries at most one access credential, presented with a fresh DPoP proof on every request it makes. A caller signed in as several DIDs builds one client per DID. Without one, `TENZRO_BEARER_JWT` and `TENZRO_DPOP_PROOF` are forwarded where a process environment exists.

#### `call`

```ts
call<T>(method: string, params?: unknown[] | Record<string, unknown>): Promise<T>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `method` | `string` |  |
| `params` | `unknown[] \| Record<string, unknown>` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<T>`

**Errors** Throws on invalid input.

#### `callWithProof`

Call `method` proving possession of `prover`'s key with a DPoP proof and no access token, as a token endpoint is called (`tenzro_refreshToken`).

```ts
callWithProof<T>(method: string, params: Record<string, unknown>, prover: DpopProver): Promise<T>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `method` | `string` |  |
| `params` | `Record<string, unknown>` |  |
| `prover` | `DpopProver` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<T>`

**Errors** Throws on invalid input.

#### `streamRoute`

POST a streamed body to a realtime route on the RPC listener and yield the server-sent events it answers with, as they arrive. The body is sent while it is produced (HTTP/2 or a runtime that streams request bodies).

```ts
streamRoute(path: string, body: AsyncIterable<Uint8Array> | Iterable<Uint8Array>): AsyncGenerator<{ event: string; data: unknown; }>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | `string` |  |
| `body` | `AsyncIterable<Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>> \| Iterable<Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>>` |  |

**Returns** `AsyncGenerator<{ event: string; data: unknown; }, any, any>`

**Errors** Throws on invalid input.

#### `get`

```ts
get<T>(path: string): Promise<T>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | `string` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<T>`

```ts

```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|

#### `postNoContent`

POST to the Web API where the node replies `204 No Content` (empty body). Parsing `response.json()` on an empty body would throw, so this variant only checks the status.

**Errors** Throws on invalid input.

#### `postWithAuth`

Authenticated POST to the Web API. The `/wallet/*` endpoints require a fresh DPoP proof per request that signs over the exact `(method, htu)` pair — only the wallet kernel can produce that proof, so the SDK accepts both the bearer JWT and the proof as explicit arguments instead of reading them from ambient env.

```ts
postWithAuth<T>(path: string, body: unknown, bearerJwt: string, dpopProof: string): Promise<T>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | `string` |  |
| `body` | `unknown` |  |
| `bearerJwt` | `string` |  |
| `dpopProof` | `string` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<T>`

**Errors** Throws on invalid input.

#### `getWithAuth`

Authenticated GET counterpart to {@link postWithAuth}.

```ts
getWithAuth<T>(path: string, bearerJwt: string, dpopProof: string): Promise<T>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | `string` |  |
| `bearerJwt` | `string` |  |
| `dpopProof` | `string` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<T>`

**Errors** Throws on invalid input.

#### `postStream`

POST a JSON body to `path` on the node's RPC origin and hand back the response unread, for callers that consume a streamed body. A non-2xx status throws the node's `{"error":{..}}` as {@link ApiError} when the body carries one. No timeout applies: a stream legitimately outlives it, so cancellation is the caller's `signal`.

```ts
postStream(path: string, body: unknown, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<Response>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | `string` |  |
| `body` | `unknown` |  |
| `signal` | `AbortSignal \| undefined` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<Response>`

**Errors** Throws on invalid input.

The transaction type a rail leg's payee sends to dispute the leg its attestor confirmed, inside the compensation window: the payee is paid the leg's reserve and the attestor's bond is slashed. `evidence` (hex) is the payee's proof that the payment did not arrive.

#### `static collateralTx`

The transaction type that posts (`post: true`) or withdraws collateral for netted plans. `asset` is the token id (32-byte hex); a withdrawal keeps what the asset's open batch's net debit needs. `agent` is a delegated agent's signed action (`{ action, signature }`) when the collateral is the agent's: a post names the asset (`0x` token id, absent for TNZO), states the amount and, off TNZO, its USD value, and counts against the asset's limits and the wei limits in its terms; a withdrawal states none and returns to its wallet.

```ts
static collateralTx(asset: string, amount: bigint, post: boolean, agent?: { action: unknown; signature: unknown; }): { SettlementPlan: { op: { post_collateral: { agent?: { action: unknown; signature: unknown; } | undefined; asset: string; amount: string; }; withdraw_collateral?: undefined; } | { withdraw_collateral: { agent?: { action: unknown; signature: unknown; } | undefined; asset: string; amount: string; }; post_collateral?: undefined; }; }; }
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `asset` | `string` |  |
| `amount` | `bigint` |  |
| `post` | `boolean` |  |
| `agent` | `{ action: unknown; signature: unknown; } \| undefined` |  |

**Returns** `{ SettlementPlan: { op: { post_collateral: { agent?: { action: unknown; signature: unknown; } \| undefined; asset: string; amount: string; }; withdraw_collateral?: undefined; } \| { withdraw_collateral: { agent?: { action: unknown; signature: unknown; } \| undefined; asset: string; amount: string; }; post_collateral?: undefined; }; }; }`

**Errors** Throws on invalid input.

### SettlementClient

### SlaClient

Validator-side SLA fault-detector inspection client. Wraps: - `tenzro_slaIssueProbe` — issue a VRF-bound liveness probe to a ModelProvider / TeeProvider DID and broadcast it on the `tenzro/sla` gossipsub topic. **Validator-only** — non-validator nodes return `-32000 SlaManager not initialized`. - `tenzro_slaListOutstandingProbes` — list every in-flight probe awaiting a response, regardless of who issued it. Used by operators to spot stuck probes whose deadline has already elapsed without a response. - `tenzro_slaGetParams` — the penalty a frozen unavailable verdict takes from a compute bond (`unavailable_penalty_wei`) and this validator's VRF public key.

#### `issueProbe`

Issue a VRF-bound liveness probe to `providerDid`. Validator-only. The issuing node computes the VRF output over `(provider_did, epoch, round)`, registers the probe in its in-memory outstanding-probe map (so a fast response cannot race the insertion), and broadcasts it on the `tenzro/sla` gossipsub topic.

```ts
issueProbe(providerDid: string, epoch: number, round: number, deadlineMs: number): Promise<SlaProbeIssued>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `providerDid` | `string` | DID of the provider being probed |
| `epoch` | `number` | Validator epoch the probe is issued in |
| `round` | `number` | Probe round within the epoch |
| `deadlineMs` | `number` | Unix-millisecond timestamp by which the provider must respond before the probe is considered missed |

**Returns** `Promise<SlaProbeIssued>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_slaIssueProbe`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_slaissueprobe)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `listOutstandingProbes`

List every in-flight probe awaiting a response from any provider, regardless of issuer. Used by operators to spot probes whose `deadline_ms` has already elapsed without a matching response.

```ts
listOutstandingProbes(): Promise<SlaOutstandingProbes>
```

**Returns** `Promise<SlaOutstandingProbes>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_slaListOutstandingProbes`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_slalistoutstandingprobes)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `getParams`

Read the fault-detector parameters this validator is using. Returns the slash threshold (missed probes before slashing fires), the per-crossing slash amount in wei, and this validator's VRF public key.

```ts
getParams(): Promise<SlaParams>
```

**Returns** `Promise<SlaParams>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_slaGetParams`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_slagetparams)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

`tenzro_slaVerdict`.


| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `params` | `{ epoch?: unknown; provider_did?: unknown; }` |  |

State-sync snapshot client for `tenzro_listSnapshots` and `tenzro_getSnapshotManifest`. Both are reads. The snapshot data itself (the anchor chain and the state buckets) is fetched over the node's iroh state-sync protocol from the listed `endpoint_id` and verified against the manifest.

The full manifest for the snapshot at `height`. Returns the node's `-32004 no snapshot at height` error if it holds none there.

### SseDecoder

Decodes a byte stream into {@link SseEvent}s. Accepts `\r\n`, `\n` and `\r` line breaks, skips `:` comment lines, and ignores unknown fields.


| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `chunk` | `Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>` |  |

**Returns** `SseEvent[]`

**Errors** Throws on invalid input.

#### `finish`

End of stream: process an unterminated last line and dispatch its event.

```ts

```

**Returns** `SseEvent[]`

**Errors** Throws on invalid input.

### StorageClient

Decentralized storage client. A node started with the `storage` role spawns a storage-provider runtime: it erasure-codes objects, publishes their shards over the content-addressed transport. A renter pays for keeping an object through a storage compute claim that commits the object's descriptor digest; each hour the claim pays the provider only if validators found its bond available, which requires a possession proof of the object. These calls target the provider node directly; they succeed only when that node is serving the storage role.

#### `storeObject`

Stores an object owned by `ownerDid`: erasure-codes `data` and publishes its shards over the transport. Only `ownerDid` may retrieve it. `signer` holds the key `ownerDid` resolves to and signs the request's envelope.

```ts
storeObject(objectId: string, owner: string, data: Uint8Array, dataShards: number, parityShards: number, ownerDid: string, signer: HybridSigner): Promise<StoredObject>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `objectId` | `string` |  |
| `owner` | `string` |  |
| `data` | `Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>` |  |
| `dataShards` | `number` |  |
| `parityShards` | `number` |  |
| `ownerDid` | `string` |  |
| `signer` | `HybridSigner` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<StoredObject>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_storageStoreObject`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_storagestoreobject)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

```typescript
const stored = await client.storage.storeObject(
  "photo-1",
  "0xowner",
  new TextEncoder().encode("hello"),
  4,
  2,
  "did:tenzro:human:alice",
  signer,
);
console.log(`stored ${stored.size_bytes} bytes`);
```

#### `retrieveObject`

Rebuilds an object from its shards for `readerDid` and returns its bytes. The object's access policy must admit `readerDid`; `signer` holds the key it resolves to and signs the request's envelope.

```ts
retrieveObject(objectId: string, readerDid: string, signer: HybridSigner): Promise<Uint8Array>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `objectId` | `string` |  |
| `readerDid` | `string` |  |
| `signer` | `HybridSigner` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_storageRetrieveObject`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_storageretrieveobject)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

Sets the provider's fixed byte-epoch rate, in wei, what deals opened from now on pay.


| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `rate` | `string \| bigint` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<Record<string, unknown>>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_storageSetPricing`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_storagesetpricing)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

### StreamingClient

Client for streaming and real-time operations. Streams chat from the node's `POST /v1/chat/completions` and opens SSE connections to A2A/MCP servers.

#### `chatStream`

Stream a chat completion as typed events: reasoning, content, tool-call deltas, finish and usage, in arrival order. An error the node reports, before or during the stream, is thrown as {@link ApiError }.

```ts
chatStream(request: ChatRequest, signal?: AbortSignal): AsyncGenerator<ChatStreamEvent>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `request` | `ChatRequest` |  |
| `signal` | `AbortSignal \| undefined` |  |

**Returns** `AsyncGenerator<ChatStreamEvent, any, any>`

**Errors** Throws on invalid input.

```typescript
const request = { model: "qwen3.5-4b", messages: [{ role: "user", content: "Hello!" }] };
for await (const event of client.streaming.chatStream(request)) {
  if (event.type === "content") process.stdout.write(event.text);
}
```

#### `chat`

Stream a chat completion, calling `onEvent` for each event, and return the assembled completion.

| `signal` | `AbortSignal \| undefined` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<ChatCompletion>`

### TenzroAgentWallet

#### `spawn`

Spawn a new autonomous-agent identity backed by a passkey-rooted smart account. The caller is responsible for producing the WebAuthn credential externally (Studio: `device_create_passkey`; browser: `navigator.credentials.create`). The node registers the identity the passkey derives and returns the account it derives. Nothing about the account is stored by the node: its keystore is the passkey alone until its first `KeystoreUpdate`. Re-calling with the same passkey, credential and salt yields the same address.

#### `getBlockRange`

Fetch a contiguous range of blocks for catch-up sync. Returns up to `maxResults` blocks (default 64, capped at 256). Use `nextHeight` and `moreAvailable` to drive pagination. `moreAvailable` reflects whether the chain has further blocks beyond `nextHeight`, independent of the requested `endHeight`, so a sync loop can step over pruning gaps: ```ts let cur = 0; while (true) { const r = await client.getBlockRange(cur, cur + 255, 256); for (const b of r.blocks) { /* ... *\/ } if (!r.moreAvailable) break; cur = r.nextHeight; } ```

```ts
getBlockRange(startHeight: number, endHeight: number, maxResults?: number): Promise<BlockRange>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `startHeight` | `number` |  |
| `endHeight` | `number` |  |
| `maxResults` | `number \| undefined` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<BlockRange>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_getBlockRange`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_getblockrange)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `getTransaction`

Get a transaction by hash. Resolves from finalized storage first, then falls back to the consensus mempool. The returned object's `status` field is `"pending"` while the transaction is in-mempool and `"finalized"` once it has been included in a block — callers polling immediately after broadcast can therefore distinguish "not yet finalized" from "unknown hash" (the RPC returns `null` only when the hash is unknown to both storage and mempool).

```ts
getTransaction(txHash: string): Promise<Transaction | null>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `txHash` | `string` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<Transaction \| null>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_getTransaction`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_gettransaction)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `getFeeHistory`

Returns base-fee history and gas-usage ratios for the last `blockCount` blocks. `newestBlock` is a hex height or `"latest"`. `rewardPercentiles` requests per-block tip percentiles (e.g. `[25, 50, 75]`); pass `undefined` to omit. `baseFeePerGas` returns `blockCount + 1` entries — the trailing entry is the predicted base fee for the next block. **Errors** Throws on invalid input.

#### `static fromInjected`

Construct a client that routes RPCs through a browser-extension provider (`window.tenzro`) discovered via EIP-6963. The Tenzro provider handles auth (DPoP-bound JWT) and CAIP-25 sessions on its own — the SDK never sees the user's keys or tokens and never opens a direct fetch to a node. All `client.rpc.call(...)` calls become `provider.request(...)` calls. Every call goes through the provider; `options.config` sets the chain id (the preview network's by default) and any REST endpoint to fetch directly. Throws if no Tenzro provider is announced within `timeoutMs` (default 3000) — wrap the call in a try/catch and render an "Install Tenzro" CTA on `TenzroNotInstalledError`.

```ts
static fromInjected(options?: { config?: TenzroConfig; timeoutMs?: number; rdns?: string; }): Promise<TenzroClient>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `options` | `{ config?: TenzroConfig; timeoutMs?: number; rdns?: string; } \| undefined` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<TenzroClient>`

**Errors** Throws on invalid input.

```ts
try {
  const client = await TenzroClient.fromInjected();
  const block = await client.getLatestBlock();
} catch (err) {
  if (err instanceof TenzroNotInstalledError) showInstallCta();
  else throw err;
}
```

### TenzroNotInstalledError

Thrown when a Tenzro provider is expected but not present in the page. Catch this in dApps to render an "Install Tenzro" CTA rather than a generic error. The `code` field is also set to the literal string `"TENZRO_NOT_INSTALLED"` for callers that prefer duck-typing over `instanceof`.

### TrustClient

Certifications, ratings, operator policies and model provenance. Every record is signed by its author on their own TPM, Secure Enclave or passkey before it reaches this client, and the node re-verifies each one, so submitting a record grants it nothing it cannot prove. Records are JSON documents (W3C Verifiable Credential 2.0 shapes with an `ecdsa-jcs-2019` proof) and are passed through unchanged.

#### `submit`

Submits a signed credential, revocation, issuer revocation, operator policy, origin attestation, model manifest or policy violation evidence. A violation proven for the first time slashes the operator's compute bond; the result reports it.


|---|---|---|
| `record` | `unknown` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<SubmitResult>`

### TypedTxClient

Signs and submits typed transactions.

#### `send`

Sign `tx` with `signer` and submit it; returns `tenzro_sendRawTransaction`'s answer.

```ts
send(signer: HybridSigner, tx: TypedTransaction): Promise<unknown>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `signer` | `HybridSigner` |  |
| `tx` | `TypedTransaction` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<unknown>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_sendRawTransaction`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_sendrawtransaction)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `sendVia`

Sign `tx` with `signer` and submit it through `method`, which takes the params `tenzro_sendRawTransaction` takes (`tenzro_revokeIdentity` for a `RevokeIdentity` transaction).

```ts
sendVia(method: string, signer: HybridSigner, tx: TypedTransaction): Promise<unknown>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `method` | `string` |  |
| `signer` | `HybridSigner` |  |
| `tx` | `TypedTransaction` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<unknown>`

**Errors** Throws on invalid input.

#### `sign`

Sign `tx` with `signer` without submitting it. Returns the signed transaction in the network's JSON form, for a party that submits it later (an x402 `plan` payment carries one; see `planPaymentPayload`).

```ts
sign(signer: HybridSigner, tx: TypedTransaction): Promise<SignedTransactionJson>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `signer` | `HybridSigner` |  |
| `tx` | `TypedTransaction` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<SignedTransactionJson>`

**Errors** Throws on invalid input.

#### `prepare`

A dry run of `tx` sent from the account `from` (32-byte hex; `tx.from` wins when set): reads the nonce, chain id and gas price the node reports, asks the node to encode the signing payload and checks that the encoding is the transaction built here. Returns the request and the digest a signer would sign; nothing is signed or submitted.

```ts
prepare(from: string, tx: TypedTransaction): Promise<PreparedTransaction>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `from` | `string` |  |
| `tx` | `TypedTransaction` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<PreparedTransaction>`

**Errors** Throws on invalid input.

### UrwaClient

ERC-7943 (uRWA) reads from chain state: whether a token's issuer halted holder transfers, and how much of a holder's balance it froze. The issuer's controls (freezing, halting, forced transfers) are `Token` transactions it signs ({@link TokenClient.operation }).

### ValidatorClient

Client for the on-chain validator registry — used by operator dashboards, SREs, validator-fleet tooling, and any client that needs to enumerate the active set, inspect a single validator's stake, activation epoch, or TEE-attestation status. Backed by the `tenzro_getValidatorState` / `tenzro_listValidators` / `tenzro_listActiveValidators` RPCs. Validator registration happens through the staking transaction path.

#### `getState`

Fetch a single validator's registry entry by 32-byte address (hex form, with or without `0x` prefix — the node decodes hex, not base58, on the request path even though responses are base58-encoded). Returns `null` if the address is not registered.

```ts
getState(address: string): Promise<ValidatorRegistryEntry | null>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `address` | `string` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<ValidatorRegistryEntry \| null>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_getValidatorState`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_getvalidatorstate)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

#### `list`

List validators in the registry, optionally filtered by status. Omit `status` to return every entry regardless of state.

```ts
list(status?: ValidatorStatus): Promise<ListValidatorsResult>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | `ValidatorStatus \| undefined` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<ListValidatorsResult>`

**Calls** [`tenzro_listValidators`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_listvalidators)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.

Convenience over `list("Active")` — returns only the validators currently producing blocks. The node returns the same shape, so the result type is identical to `list()`.

**Returns** `Promise<ListValidatorsResult>`

### WalletClient

Client for wallet operations. Supports permissionless hardware-key wallets and standard accounts.

#### `getBalance`

Get the native token balance (TNZO) for an address. Returns balance as bigint (in smallest unit).

```ts
getBalance(address: Address): Promise<bigint>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `address` | `string` |  |

#### `sendSelfCustody`

Sign a TNZO transfer with a hardware {@link HybridSigner} and submit it via `tenzro_sendRawTransaction`; the node never holds the key. The account of the signer's P-256 key is the `from` account. This method fetches the nonce and chain id, builds the canonical `Transaction::hash()` preimage, has the hardware sign its composite representative, and submits the pre-signed transaction. The node requires the ML-DSA-65 leg when the account enrolled an ML-DSA-65 key.

```ts
sendSelfCustody(args: { signer: HybridSigner; to: Address; value: bigint; from?: Address; gasLimit?: number; gasPrice?: number; nonce?: number; chainId?: number; acknowledgeRecipient?: string; }): Promise<string>
```

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `args` | `{ signer: HybridSigner; to: Address; value: bigint; from?: Address; gasLimit?: number; gasPrice?: number; nonce?: number; chainId?: number; acknowledgeRecipient?: string; }` |  |

**Returns** `Promise<string>` The submitted transaction hash (64-char lowercase hex).

**Calls** [`tenzro_getNonce`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_getnonce), [`eth_chainId`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#eth_chainid), [`tenzro_sendRawTransaction`](https://github.com/tenzro/tenzro-network/blob/main/docs/RPC.md#tenzro_sendrawtransaction)

**Errors** Rejects with `RpcCallError` carrying the node's JSON-RPC error code and message.
